textPlacement.assessment: The topic row and full entry consistently describe Davies’s shared care perspective, including help and partial participation. The full entry correctly distinguishes sink washing (appendix 14+) from the separate table variant (18+, able to carry a jug, interested in repeating sink washing), and does not turn the latter into a required home setup. Soap/towel, hair/nose care and the quoted reference locators are supported. The earlier 12–18 chart is explicitly cumulative into the later column; the broader care-of-self caption from 15 months does not invalidate the specifically identified appendix sink row. The 18–24 placement fits the source context without promising a milestone.

Both topic rows carry the same supported ordinary invitation to use a cloth alongside an adult with help. The full entry preserves manageable tools, a sweeping guide as an example, process over finish, stopping before overwhelm and shared return. Sweeping/dusting 16–18+ and earlier spill wiping 12–18 are correct chart/appendix labels. It does not import the separate walking-conditioned table-wiping setup or later table-washing protocol, and does not prescribe supplies or a completed chore.

Both topic summaries retain Davies attribution, adult help, manageable tools, steady walking for the watering example and already-cut flower stems. The full entry adds the supported sponge/plant duster, pots without a garden, small vase/jug/funnel, spill sponge, partial pouring/wiping and shared supervised gardening. The source’s optional complete arrangement is not made compulsory. Watering 14+ with steady walking and flowers/seeds 18+ match the original rows; the 18–24 display adds no new developmental deadline or required garden.

issues.surface: RENDERED_SURFACES.json surfaces[placementId="18-24.toddler-food-preparation"].entryText; EntryReading full-entry detail. The topicRows summaries are not the affected surface.
issues.finding: The sentence “She keeps sharp knives out of reach until the child is ready and an adult can supervise” reduces the kitchen passage to a general readiness-plus-supervision access condition in an 18–24-month entry. PDF 77 separately says to keep sharp knives out of reach, and its preceding tool progression describes sharper knives with a cutting guide as children become preschoolers, with supervision. The compressed “until” wording loses both that age/tool context and the distinction between storage and an adult showing use; it can be read as a broader permission for sharp knives in this browsing band.
issues.requiredCorrection: Revise only the affected descriptive passage to preserve the source’s separate out-of-reach instruction and its preschooler/cutting-guide example. For example: “Davies requires supervision for activities with sharp tools. Her kitchen section keeps sharp knives out of reach and describes introducing sharper knives with a cutting guide as children become preschoolers, with supervision. Preparing food remains something to do together.” Retain the current supported salad-leaf summary and the explicit apple-example distinction; do not turn this into a new knife-use protocol or add outside care advice.

textPlacement.assessment: The two topic rows are supported: Davies includes small supervised contributions, and tearing/rinsing salad leaves is explicitly supported at PDF 99 and the under-two practical-life discussion. The full entry preserves tools for small hands, initial help, wandering off, low/dining-table alternatives and the different apple examples (18 months–3 years assisted chart versus from-2-years illustrated caption; appendix 18+). Its final sharp-knife sentence needs the specific correction below before the text/placement component can pass. This is a full-detail fidelity issue; it does not require removing the food-preparation topic or adding outside advice.

The topic rows and full entry accurately combine visible few complete activities, grouped pieces, an undone puzzle, storage of currently unused/difficult materials, rotation when interest/challenge changes and shared return. The full source provides no fixed activity count or rotation calendar for this guidance. Davies’s own return of an earlier activity while the child concentrates on the next is preserved. The general age statement is supported by the independently read PDF 33 context in the private age basis; no precise shelf milestone is implied by the 18–24 retrieval band.

Both topic rows and full text preserve the meaningful condition that older children’s small parts are actually inaccessible to younger children, rather than merely placed higher. The proposed simplification is a distinct supported way to participate and is not permission to expose small parts. Personal belongings, privacy, voluntary alone space, shared-room agreements and fewer displayed items/useful storage come from the cited full home unit. The distinction from sending an upset toddler away is consistent with the separately read cooperation/tantrum context and does not import its older-child calm-place example. The toddler-wide 1–3 scope matches PDF 14 and remains situation-based.

Both topic rows and the full entry preserve a small useful shared shopping contribution, with source examples of a picture list and checkout belt, optional continuing participation in unpacking, manageable demands and adult help. The waiting/transition cue and movement/connection qualification match the full cooperation context, including its continuation beyond the cited 123–125 span. The invitation promises neither occupation for the entire outing nor compliance. The source’s 18 months–3 years supermarket row fits this retrieval band; the general indicative-age wording is supported by PDF 33 in the private age basis.
